items.title: Simple models outperform single-cell foundation models on downstream benchmarks
items.why: Tests single-cell foundation models against simple linear pipelines on benchmarks commonly used to evaluate them.
items.takeaway: The authors report state-of-the-art or near-state-of-the-art results from careful normalization plus linear methods, including on novel cell types and organisms.

items.title: Trying to Cure My Cystic Fibrosis
items.why: A first-person explanation of why CFTR modulators miss patients with no CFTR protein, and why gene therapy and editing delivery to the lung is so hard. It covers mucus, cell types, viral vectors and lipid nanoparticles. The excerpt is cut off, and clinical details such as the 4DMT data are the author's account.
items.takeaway: Nonsense and frameshift CFTR variants leave modulator drugs with no protein to act on, which is why the author works on gene therapy.

items.title: Stop using win rate: comparing model rankings across different benchmark tasks
items.why: A short, practical critique of win rate as a benchmark metric, with code for within-task statistical tests, rank aggregation and a Friedman test. It pairs well with the single-cell benchmark preprint. The worked example uses simulated data, not real model results.
items.takeaway: A model can have a high win rate yet be statistically inseparable from others or fail badly on some tasks.

items.title: Diffusion is spectral autoregression
items.why: Uses spectral analysis to show that diffusion on images behaves like approximate autoregression in frequency space, with a reproducible Colab notebook.
items.takeaway: Natural image spectra follow a power law, so adding noise acts like a low-pass filter whose cut-off depends on the noise variance.

items.title: The AlphaFold2 Method Paper: A Fount of Good Ideas
items.why: A close reading of AlphaFold2's architecture that pulls out design lessons for molecular ML, such as the 1D sequence representation, information flow and triangular attention. It is one researcher's interpretation; the post itself says it may be wrong.
items.takeaway: The author argues that a 1D representation coupled to a pairwise 2D one is what lets the structure be read out.

items.title: The Future of Protein Science will not be Supervised
items.why: Argues that learning representations of protein sequence space is a strong setting for semi-supervised learning, because sequences far outnumber labels. It is a 2019 opinion piece about a preprint, so read the later literature before relying on its claims.
items.takeaway: The UniRep authors report that next-amino-acid prediction yielded representations useful across tasks, including a neuron that partly separates helices from strands.

items.title: Visual Information Theory
items.why: A visual foundation for probability, codes and entropy that underlies cross-entropy and KL-style reasoning in generative models.
items.takeaway: Variable-length codes trade codeword length against probability, and entropy is the minimum average length (1.75 bits in the example).

items.title: Feature Visualization
items.by: Chris Olah, Alexander Mordvintsev, Ludwig Schubert
items.why: A rigorous, hands-on explanation of feature visualization by optimization, covering diversity, regularization and how neurons interact. It adds an interpretability thread to a list that is otherwise mostly generative modelling and protein ML. The examples come from InceptionV1.
items.takeaway: The authors note that neurons are not necessarily the right semantic units for understanding networks.
